Hey Product Hunt! 👋 I'm Ramana, founder of Youkti.

We are here to change the GTM and sales industry.   
  
Youkti is an AI-enabled revenue action platform that remembers every account and tells your sales team what to do next. The data layer is free.

Problem: Sales teams pay a fortune for data and still don't know what to do with it. Every feed metered by the credit, and a rep still opens their CRM on Monday guessing which account to work. Meanwhile deals slip quietly and nobody notices until the quarter closes. [...] Solution: Youkti keeps a running memory of every account, conversation, and deal, then turn it into a daily list of specific moves. Which deal is at risk and why. Which dormant account just fired a signal. Which renewal needs a call before it's too late. Which stakeholder joined tomorrow's meeting and what you need ready.

What makes us different: Youkti gives the data away. Our take is that data got cheap and good enough for everyone, so owning it stopped being an advantage. The hard part is knowing what to do next, and that's what Youkti excels at.

Free, no card, no trial clock, no usage meter:

@iamanantgupta Central question, and it's how the whole thing earns trust. By default Zaro reaches for the context relevant to what you're describing, looking across your connected sources and pulling what relates to the task rather than dumping everything in, weighing relevance, recency, and source as it goes.

And yes, there's a manual layer, which we think matters a lot. It's not meant to be a black box you just hope got it right. You can see what it's drawing on and steer it: point it at specific sources, scope what's included, exclude what you don't want. Automatic by default, hands on the wheel whenever you want them there.

@iamanantgupta   
  
By default, Zaro pulls the context that's relevant to what you're asking for. When you describe what you want to build, it looks across your connected sources and pulls in what relates to that task rather than dumping everything in. Relevance, recency, and source all factor into what it reaches for.

On manual control, yes, that layer matters a lot to us. The goal is never a black box where you just hope it grabbed the right things. You can see what context it's drawing on and steer it, point it at specific sources, scope it to what you want included, and exclude what you don't. Automatic by default, but with you in the driver's seat when you want to be.

Yannis here, also on the team.

Adding a bit to what Michael said. The thing that got me excited about Zaro wasn't any single feature, it was watching what happened after teams started using it for a couple of weeks. The work it takes over isn't the flashy stuff, it's the quiet drag that nobody puts on a roadmap but everybody feels. The follow-up that slips, the report that takes an afternoon to pull together, the handoff between two tools that someone has to babysit.
